Replay

Restoring a published checkpoint

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Client sequenceAuthority and storage contractValidation and integration status

Use a Restore decision when no live authority remains and a trusted member needs to resume a published checkpoint. Checkpoint protocol 3 retains the explicit Restore decision introduced in version 2 and adds complete asset-package transfer. Upload/download do not grant authority. A restore selects one exact durable publication and obtains a new authority epoch only after current membership, policy, lease and storage checks. The private Bundle/Record and gameplay/checkpoint formats remain unchanged.

Client sequence#

  1. Recover the existing enrollment credentials, then register the fresh process through the authority RPC Challenge/Rebind handshake on the same connection. The checkpoint-enabled service permits replacement of an expired owner's incarnation only after lease expiry and coordinator restart quarantine. A live owner is still protected. Registration preserves the stable game token and grants no lease; the old owner identity remains in the record until a restore or another authorized migration decision wins.
  2. Read status and download the selected publication through the checkpoint client. client_prepare performs typed checkpoint validation and copies it into an owned authority.Prepared. Keep that owner at a stable address. Prepare every required external game asset before requesting authority.
  3. Call client_restore with the current authority Lease, exact Publication and owned Prepared. No ordinary authority RPC may be pending simultaneously. Restore uses that Lease's request sequence; normal upload/download operation sequences remain separate. Continue multiplexing checkpoint and authority replies.
  4. A successful correlated reply installs a lease for the new epoch and sets its require_owner flag. Check lease_live before restoring: a delayed successful decision can arrive with no usable lease time. Use prepared_restore or the equivalent Session path with that lease/permit and the correct local seat. Supply Resume_Options.local_incarnation for a fresh process; Session forwards a nonzero Session_Options.incarnation. Zero retains legacy saved incarnation behavior, and a supplied older incarnation is rejected before runtime creation.
Odin
publication := client.saved.publication
error := checkpoint.client_prepare(&client, &prepared, game_model)
// Check error; prepare referenced assets before continuing.
error = checkpoint.client_restore(&client, &lease, publication, &prepared)
// Pump the shared control connection. After a successful reply and live lease:
restore_error := authority.prepared_restore(
    &prepared, &server, game_model, gameplay_wire, &lease, local_seat,
    options = {local_incarnation = lease.identity.incarnation},
)

This abbreviated example omits application error/UI handling. Client close or failure cancels its outstanding lease request, not a possibly committed authority decision. Keep Prepared until the chosen restore/retry outcome is resolved.

Authority and storage contract#

service_recover_published is a trusted integration entry point. The protocol server verifies HMAC, exact request context and current identity/nonce/peer/ connection/coordinator-generation binding before calling the backend. The backend must atomically guard the authority commit against publication replacement; this entry point is not a public function that authenticates arbitrary raw arguments.

The SQLite adapter loads and validates the deployment-selected model, then holds the exact publication as a scoped commit guard. The existing provisioning commit reloads the publication inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE and compares all its metadata, including revision and Point. The private Bundle, new authority epoch, recovered Point and restore request frontier commit together through the existing Room callback. No second in-memory Bundle can diverge from the service's Record.

Restore requires:

  • An enabled trusted host. Dedicated policy additionally requires infrastructure.
  • A current playable reservation for the actor's stable token in a cooperative checkpoint, with no matching game ban. A merely enrolled peer cannot take another player's local seat. Dedicated infrastructure uses the dedicated local-seat path.
  • An expired owner lease and elapsed restart quarantine. A concurrent live owner renewal or a different coordinator process is fenced by the durable Record CAS.
  • The exact latest publication revision, model contract and Point. A checkpoint in the current epoch is allowed. A prior grant's exact recovered Point remains eligible after that grant/service was lost without a newer publication; arbitrary older points are refused.
  • The existing max_known_rollback bound and final-release constraint. A save can be durable yet too old to authorize. Set save cadence and deployment recovery policy deliberately; publication alone does not override that policy.

The primitive stages the grant with existing coordinator rules, then persists the request result. Admitted policy refusals such as Busy and Too_Old also persist their frontier, so replay after expiry cannot turn the same rejected request into a grant. Malformed/unauthorized requests and unavailable/mismatched publications are rejected before this decision admission. A later explicit request uses a new lease sequence and is evaluated against the then-current state.

An exact lost grant reply returns the durable result without advancing epoch or renewing its lease. A higher RPC frontier makes an older request stale. If the coordinator restarts, its usual generation advance/quarantine still applies; a fresh registered process may need a newer grant using the same exact retained source Point. Old traffic cannot resurrect the earlier epoch.

While the endpoint remains live, an exact request whose digest/result still matches the durable frontier uses a cached receipt plus a freshly calculated authority view. It does not repeat model/asset decoding or block a queued lease renewal. Stale frontiers are rejected before storage loading. Cache loss still uses the validated storage path; the cache itself never establishes authority.

allow_expired_owner_rebind is a trusted service opt-in installed while an attached checkpoint endpoint has a recovery backend. Closing that endpoint restores its previous setting. Services without recovery support retain the former blanket owner-rebind refusal. The opt-in does not itself check or grant a saved-world claim.

Validation and integration status#

Low-level callers should refresh a successful Restore grant with a new correlated authority Renew before paying runtime setup costs. The Restore request may spend much of its lifetime in transfer/validation, and its local lease deadline is anchored to request start. Even an already expired local permit can request renewal; only the coordinator decides whether the reservation still exists. Installation and simulation still require a live permit. Room handles this exchange automatically. The delayed-grant gate covers both a successful same-epoch renewal and an expired-reservation refusal.

Native TLS fixtures restore the three actual Cavecrawl, Speedball and Scrapyard models after all original client processes and the service have exited: incarnation 2 receives epoch 2 and advances a saved tick-1 simulation to tick 11. Unit tests cover stale traffic, lease/quarantine, excessive rollback, missing playable seats, lost grants, rejected-request replay, storage Point/publication substitution and dedicated infrastructure/final-release rules. Real processes killed before/after the restore commit recover respectively epoch 1/request 2 or epoch 2/request 3, while publication 1 remains intact; fresh coordinator startup is inactive.

Godot Room/Party drives the complete download/preparation/restore lifecycle and Cavecrawl exposes resume/retry UI. Separate native and browser gates resume actual saved cave play and accept new guests after all original processes have exited. Room distinguishes service-known rollback from local confirmation history. Atomic asset packages cover declared dependencies including Scrapyard sprays. Broader asset profiles, other game acceptance and broader loss reporting remain integration work. See Room restoration and the M5 plan.
